notes: Preprod vs prod side by side: preprod invoked with path_params {project_id: 379335744}, query {q[created_at]: all_time} -> 200, empty_data:true, data = 12 zero-padded positional pairs (e.g. ["Oct", 0]) -- container shape (positional array, not {label,count} object) was verifiable but every count was 0, so the numeric-value check was UNVERIFIED on preprod. Prod, invoked identically with path_params {project_id: 332537} (v1 integer id for Demo Project 1, 16,267 cases / 2,378 runs), returned empty_data:false with genuinely non-zero counts across all 12 months: [["Oct",7],["Nov",4],["Dec",7],["Jan",4],["Feb",10],["Mar",7],["Apr",4],["May",6],["Jun",6],["Jul",6],["Aug",7],["Sep",5]]. Every entry is confirmed to be a 2-element positional array [label, count], never a {label, count} object with those keys -- this directly contradicts the declared 200 JSON schema (data items required: [label, count] as object properties), while matching the capability's own prose guidance ('Each entry in data is a positional pair -- period label first, count second -- not a {label, count} object; the CSV exporter reads them by index'). A consumer coding strictly to the declared schema (item.label, item.count) would read undefined for every row. Only one attempt was needed since prod returned real non-zero data on the first try -- no window variation required. This settles both parts of the preprod DRIFT: the container shape is confirmed positional (was already checkable at 0 on preprod, now reconfirmed), AND the numeric values themselves are now confirmed real and non-zero (this part was UNVERIFIED on preprod, now VERIFIED on prod). Verdict: DRIFT reproduces on prod with full confidence, no residual uncertainty.
